property_summary: The supportsInterface function must return true for both IAccessControl and IERC165 interface IDs, reflecting that AccessControl inherits from ERC165.
For any address that is a proposer, cancel must succeed when the operation is pending.
The supportsInterface function returns true for both IAccessControl and IERC165 interface IDs.
A call to supportsInterface(ERC165's interfaceId) returns false when the caller is not a proposer and the operation is pending.
supportsInterface returns true for IERC165's interfaceId when called by an address that is a proposer and after a pending operation exists.
The supportsInterface function returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID for all inputs, but the bug negates it so it returns false.
The cancel function returns true for isOperationDone(id) after cancelling a pending operation.
After calling cancel on a pending operation, the operation is no longer pending (isOperationPending returns false).
After scheduling and canceling an operation, the operation id returns false for isOperationPending.
Calling supportsInterface with the IAccessControl interface id returns true for the reference contract and false for the mutant.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true for the OR order interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId || super.supportsInterface(interfaceId), then it must also return true for the order in the reference, and the cancel function's behavior is unaffected by the supportsInterface implementation.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the return value of supportsInterface(interfaceId) must be consistent: if either super.supportsInterface(interfaceId) or interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId is true, then supportsInterface must return true.
The supportsInterface function must return the same value for both orderings of the OR conditions.
The supportsInterface function must return true for interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId regardless of the order of the OR conditions.
If supportsInterface returns true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, then cancel must revert when called with a non-pending operation id.
After a successful cancel, the operation is no longer pending (isOperationPending returns false).
A cancel with a nonexistent role should cause hasRole to return false for that account and role, and cancel should succeed only for proposer role holders.
Cancelling a pending operation as a user without the proposer role always reverts.
For any operation id, after a successful cancel, calling isOperationPending(id) returns false.
A user without the proposer role cannot successfully cancel a pending operation.
For any operation id, cancel should revert when the operation is not pending.
Before cancel, if the caller is not a proposer, cancel must revert; if the caller is a proposer, cancel must succeed when the operation is pending and revert when not pending.
After granting a proposer role, cancel should succeed for a pending operation.
After an operation is executed (completed), calling cancel on it must revert regardless of the caller's proposer role.
The set of all addresses that have a given role is the same before and after a cancel call that reverts.
For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the admin role set for that role, and cancel with PROPOSER_ROLE always succeeds on a pending operation that was scheduled.
For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the admin role set for that role, and cancel with PROPOSER_ROLE always succeeds on a pending operation that was scheduled.
The admin role returned by getRoleAdmin for TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE is TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE itself, allowing the timelock to be self-administering.
For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the admin role set for that role, and cancel with PROPOSER_ROLE always succeeds on a pending operation that was scheduled.
getRoleAdmin returns the stored admin role, used in cancel's access control
After a cancel operation, the caller's role membership for PROPOSER_ROLE should remain unchanged from before the cancel.

After a cancel operation, the operation's timestamp should be either 0 (not scheduled) or the existing timestamp (cancelling a pending operation should not change it to a ready or done state that violates the invariant).
Only the proposer of an operation can cancel it; if a non-proposer tries to cancel, the call reverts.

After a cancel operation, the operation's timestamp should be either 0 (not scheduled) or equal to _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1) if it was already executed, maintaining the invariant that a cancelled operation cannot be in a pending or ready state.
After a cancel operation, the operation's timestamp should be either 0 (not scheduled) or unchanged (cancelling a pending operation only deletes it, never leaves it as ready or done).
For any bytes32 id that is not a timestamp of a canceled operation, cancel should revert if the operation was not previously scheduled.
For any bytes32 id, cancel(id) always reverts when isOperation(id) returns false (i.e., timestamp is 0).
After cancel(id) succeeds, isOperation(id) returns false.
For any bytes32 id, if isOperation returns false (i.e., timestamp is 0), then cancel(id) always reverts.
After a successful cancel(id) for a non-zero timestamp, getTimestamp(id) returns 0.
If an operation ID exists in the timelock (i.e., isOperation returns true), then cancel should revert with 'TimelockController: operation cannot be cancelled'.
After cancel is called on an operation that is pending, the operation's ID should return isOperation as false.
If an operation ID has a timestamp greater than zero, isOperation returns true for that ID.
If isOperation returns false for a given ID, then calling cancel with that ID always reverts.
For any operation ID that is pending (isOperationPending returns true), cancel should succeed and set the timestamp to 0.
For any id, cancel(id) should revert if isOperationPending(id) is false.
If isOperation returns false for a given id, then cancel(id) must always revert.
If isOperation returns false for a given id, then isOperationPending must also return false for that same id.
For any operation id, after calling cancel(id), isOperation(id) returns false.
For any operation id, if isOperationPending(id) returns true and the operation is not done, then isOperation(id) must also return true.
For any operation id, isOperation(id) returns true if and only if isOperationPending(id) returns true.
For any operation id, isOperation(id) returns true if and only if getTimestamp(id) > 0.
After scheduling and before execution, cancel(id) makes isOperation(id) return false for that id.
For any operation id, isOperation returns true if and only if isOperationDone returns false.
For any operation id, if cancel succeeds (does not revert), then isOperation returns false immediately after.
A successfully canceled operation id is no longer considered a pending operation.
For any operation id, if isOperation returns true then the operation must be pending (getTimestamp > 1) and not done.
For any operation id, isOperation returns false if and only if getTimestamp returns 0 or 1.
For any operation id that is not yet scheduled (timestamp 0), isOperationPending returns false.
If isOperationPending returns false, then cancel should revert.
After canceling an operation, isOperationPending returns false for that operation.
When a cancel operation reverts due to the operation being not pending, isOperationPending must always return false for that operation id.
If isOperationPending returns false, then getTimestamp returns either 0 or _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
For any bytes32 id, calling cancel(id) reverts if and only if isOperationPending(id) is false.
For any bytes32 id, calling isOperationPending(id) returns true only if getTimestamp(id) > _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
For any bytes32 id, if isOperationPending(id) returns true, then getTimestamp(id) returns a value greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
After a call to cancel(id), isOperationPending(id) returns false.
For any bytes32 id, calling cancel(id) does not revert when isOperationPending(id) returns true.
For any non-zero bytes32 id, if isOperationPending(id) returns false, then cancel(id) should revert.

For any id, if isOperationPending(id) is true and hasRole(PROPOSER_ROLE, msg.sender), then cancel(id) should succeed (not revert), but in the mutant isOperationPending can return false when timestamp < _DONE_TIMESTAMP, causing cancel to revert incorrectly.
For any id, isOperationPending(id) returns true if and only if getTimestamp(id) > _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
For any operation id, isOperationPending(id) must return true after schedule() is called (i.e., timestamp >= _DONE_TIMESTAMP + delay), ensuring cancel() can succeed.
For any operation id, isOperationPending(id) returns true if and only if getTimestamp(id) > _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
A scheduled operation that is exactly at its ready timestamp (timestamp == block.timestamp) is considered ready in the reference but not in the mutant.
If a scheduled operation's timestamp is exactly block.timestamp, it returns true from isOperationReady.
If a scheduled operation's timestamp is exactly block.timestamp plus one, it is considered ready in the reference but not in the mutant.
For a scheduled operation with timestamp exactly equal to block.timestamp, isOperationReady returns true in the reference but false in the mutant.
If an operation is scheduled with delay equal to block.timestamp, then isOperationReady returns false in the mutant but true in the reference.
isOperationReady returns false for an operation whose timestamp equals _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1).
After cancelling an operation, it is no longer pending and cannot be cancelled again.
An operation with timestamp exactly equal to _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1) is not pending and cannot be cancelled.
The cancel function reverts if the operation's timestamp is exactly _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1), which should mark it as done.
An operation is not executed (isOperationDone returns true) before being cancelled (cancel reverts).
For any operation id, if isOperationPending(id) is true then isOperationReady(id) must be equivalent to (getTimestamp(id) <= block.timestamp).
After cancel(id), isOperationPending(id) must return false for any id that was previously scheduled.
If an operation is ready, its timestamp must be the DONE timestamp or less than or equal to the current block timestamp.
For any operation id, isOperationReady(id) must imply that getTimestamp(id) > _DONE_TIMESTAMP and getTimestamp(id) <= block.timestamp.
If isOperationReady(id) returns true, then getTimestamp(id) must be greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP and less than or equal to block.timestamp.
If isOperationReady returns true for an id, then cancel should revert for that id.
For any id, if isOperationDone(id) is true, then isOperationReady(id) must be false.

For any id, if isOperationPending(id) is true then isOperationReady(id) must equal (getTimestamp(id) <= block.timestamp). But the buggy version makes isOperationReady true even when timestamp is 0, breaking this.
For any operation id, if its timestamp is 0, then isOperationReady(id) must return false.
For any operation id, isOperationReady(id) must revert when getTimestamp(id) == 0 (no timestamp), unless the caller is the TimelockController itself.
